service.description: The mail accounts a user (the current user by default; another user only with authorization disabled) reaches: owned ones and those with a current EmailAccountUser row, not removed. Each account map has its fields (no server credentials), isOwner, level (1 read, 2 send, 3 manage), permissionEnumId, canSend (send level on an account that is not internal) and canManage; the Internal account is first. accessMap is emailAccountId to level. With emailAccountId, level and account are that account's (level 0 and account null when the user does not reach it). includeRemoved also lists the user's own removed accounts (EasRemoved, whose mail was kept), last, with isRemoved true, level 0, nothing they may do but delete them (canDelete, delete#EmailAccount) and keptMessageCount; they are never in accessMap, and no member reaches one.
The user's Internal account (the current user's; another user's only with authorization disabled), made the first time it is asked for. It has no server and no EmailMessage rows.

A mail account of the current user, with its Inbox, Drafts, Sent, Archive, Junk and Trash folders and a default identity of its address. The server settings make a new EmailServer the account owns (none when no host is given); emailServerId names an existing server instead, and ownerUserId another owner, only for internal work (authorization disabled). The Internal account is made by ensure#InternalAccount. recordFilingEnumId defaults by kind: an external account files only what is linked (ErfLinkedOnly), a hosted or shared one every party match (ErfAllMatches). smtpUsername (with smtpPassword, else mailPassword) is the outgoing server's own sign-in, for a provider whose SMTP takes another user than its IMAP or POP; empty, SMTP signs in as mailUsername. statusId EasPaused makes an account the sync job leaves until its setup is done (update#EmailAccount makes it active).

parameter.name: statusId
parameter.description: EasActive or EasPaused

parameter.name: displayName
parameter.description: The default identity's name; the account name, else the user's name

parameter.name: storeProtocol
parameter.description: imaps (the default), imap, pop3s or pop3

service.description:
Change an account (manage permission). A field given is set; an empty one is cleared. The server settings change the server the account owns, or make one when it has none; a server shared with others is never changed here. An empty mailPassword or smtpPassword keeps the one stored; an empty smtpUsername makes SMTP sign in as the store does again (its smtpPassword is cleared). statusId may be set to EasActive or EasPaused. The Internal account takes only its name, color and sequence.
accountKindEnumId changes the kind among hosted, external (personal) and shared: to shared at any time (the owner stays, managing it), from shared only when one person is left on it (the owner and no other current member; with no owner, the one member left becomes the owner). The filing policy follows the new kind's default (an external account files only what is linked, the others every match), unless recordFilingEnumId is given or the account's policy was not its kind's default.

Remove an account (manage permission; not the Internal account). A provider sign-in of a server it owns is revoked at the provider (revoke#OAuthToken). By default the local copies are kept: the account is EasRemoved, which no list shows, its members' rows end, and the stored password and token of a server it owns are cleared, while its messages stay for the records they are filed on. deleteLocalCopies deletes its messages, folders, labels, identities, rules, out-of-office, members, the server it owns and the account itself; a message that another record still refers to is kept, out of the account. An account removed before with its mail kept (get#EmailAccountAccess includeRemoved) is deleted only by its owner, and always with its mail (deleteLocalCopies); to anyone else it is not found.

Internal (authorization disabled), for delete#EmailAccount: delete every message of an account, a batch at a time in its own transaction. When a batch fails it goes again one message at a time; a message that cannot be deleted (a record refers to it) is taken out of the account and kept.

The current user's accounts for the Inbox rail and MailAccounts: the Internal account first (made when missing), then their own and shared accounts (get#EmailAccountAccess). Each has unreadCount (its Inbox, not snoozed; null for the Internal account, whose messages the app counts), draftCount, outboxCount and outboxErrorCount (sends that failed), its folderList ({emailFolderId, folderName, folderPath, parentFolderId, folderKindEnumId, unreadCount, totalCount (the server's, from the last sync)}, in kind and sequence order), labelList and identityList.
Share an account with a user (manage permission; not the Internal account), or change their permission: EapRead, EapSend or EapManage.
End a user's access to an account: by a manager, or the user leaving it.

Whether an account's server settings work (manage permission): org.moqui.impl.EmailServices.test#EmailServer on its server, step by step: SMTP connect and sign-in; the store's sign-in and, for IMAP, its folder list. An account that was EasAuthFailed or EasError is Active again when every step passes. smtpUsername and smtpPassword, when given, are the SMTP sign-in tried instead of the stored one (nothing is stored; an empty smtpUsername tries the store's). Each folder of folderList has folderKindEnumId, the kind the account maps it to when it has that folder (the user's choice, update#EmailFolder), else the server's (INBOX, its special use), serverKindEnumId the server's, and emailFolderId and subscribed when the account has it.

Send a test message from an account to its own address (send permission; not the Internal account), through its SMTP server as a message the user sends (deliver#DraftMessage), from its default identity. The subject starts with "[Test]". Sent, it is in Sent, and the next sync brings it to the Inbox, which shows the account both sends and receives. A send that fails answers sent false with sendError and leaves nothing in the Outbox: the test message is removed.

parameter.name: emailMessageId
parameter.description: The test message, when it was sent

service.description: A folder of an account (manage permission), under parentFolderId when given. Local for now: the sync (M5d) creates it on the server through push#RemoteChanges.
Rename a folder (manage permission); not an Inbox.

Map a folder (manage permission): folderKindEnumId makes it the account's Drafts, Sent, Archive, Junk or Trash (EfkDrafts, EfkSent, EfkArchive, EfkJunk, EfkTrash), the one of that kind: the folder that was it becomes an Other folder (one kept only here with no mail, such as the one made with the account, is deleted). The choice is the user's (kindByUser): the sync keeps it, and no server folder becomes that kind by its special use or name. Each kind stays on one folder, so a special folder is moved by choosing another one; the Inbox is the server's INBOX and does not move. subscribed N stops the sync reading the folder (its mail here stays), Y reads it again; the Inbox is always read. sequenceNum orders it among its kind.

parameter.name: formerFolderId
parameter.description: The folder that had the kind, now an Other folder or deleted

service.description: A label of an account, including the Internal account (manage permission); the name is unique in the account. An internal message is labeled with it through mantle.party.communication.CommunicationEventPartyLabel.
Rename, recolor or reorder a label (manage permission).
Delete a label and take it off its messages (manage permission).

The Inbox search line as find#Messages reads it, Gmail's operators taken out of the free text: from:, to: (To, Cc or Bcc), cc:, bcc:, subject:, has:attachment, label:, in: (inbox, sent, drafts, scheduled, outbox, snoozed, flagged or starred, archive, spam or junk, trash, all, anywhere, or a folder by name or path), is: (unread, read, flagged or starred, answered, snoozed), before: and after: (a date as 2026/10/19, 2026-10-19 or 10/19/2026), older_than: and newer_than: (2d, 3w, 6m, 1y), larger: and smaller: (bytes, or with K or M; size: is larger:) and filename: (an attachment's name). A value may be quoted (subject:"weekly report") or in parentheses (from:(ada lovelace)), and a leading - negates a term (-from:noreply, -label:news, -is:unread, -word). The rest is the free text: words, "quoted phrases", and -excluded words. A name: that is not an operator stays a word (http://example.com). A term whose value is not understood (before:someday, is:purple, has:boat) is an error naming it. termList is the operators in order, each {operator, value, negate}, for the query chips.

parameter.name: freeText
parameter.description: The words and phrases, as written, without the operators

service.description:
The current user's mail, newest first, as threads (threadMode, the default: the root message and its replies, grouped by rootEmailMessageId) or as messages, over the accounts the user reaches (emailAccountId or emailAccountIdList narrows them; the Internal account has none).
Views: inbox (the default: the Inbox folders, not archived, not snoozed until snoozedThruDate), flagged, snoozed, scheduled (ES_SCHEDULED), outbox (ES_SCHEDULED and ES_READY: waiting, held for undo, or failed), drafts, sent, archive, junk, trash, all (all but junk and trash), anywhere (all with junk and trash), folder (emailFolderId) and label (emailLabelId). Filters: unreadOnly, flaggedOnly, hasAttachment, fromAddress, toAddress (to or cc), subject, fromDate and thruDate (the message date), minSize and maxSize (bytes), and searchText, the Inbox search line: its operators (parse#SearchText: from:, to:, subject:, has:attachment, label:, in:, is:, before:, after:, larger: and the others) are conditions here, an in: choosing the view (or the folders of that name), and its free text (every word, the last one as a prefix, each "phrase", none of the -words) is searched in the MoquiEmailMessage document of the search index (subject, from, to, cc, body and labels; read searchLimit matches at a time, 2000 by default, newest first from the page's cursor, so a view with any number of matches pages) when search is configured and the index is there; otherwise, or when the search fails (logged), each word must be in the subject, body or addresses (LIKE). searchMode says which ran: index or text. The search is a view like any other (the Inbox passes view all for a search, as Gmail searches all mail), and both the search and the find are limited to the accounts the user reaches.
Paging: pageSize rows, then beforeDate, the sortDate of the last row shown (nextBeforeDate), for the next page. A row is {store (email), threadId and rootEmailMessageId (the root's id), lastEmailMessageId (the thread's newest), emailMessageId, emailAccountId, emailFolderId, folderKindEnumId and statusId (of the newest message in the view), subject, snippet, sortDate (epoch millis: the date of the thread's newest message in the view), lastDate, firstDate, messageCount, replyCount, unreadCount, isUnread, isFlagged, isArchived, snoozedThruDate, scheduledSendDate, hasAttachment, draftCount, fromAddress and fromName (of the newest message), participantList ({address, name}), participantAddressList, labelList ({emailLabelId, labelName, color}), sendError, fromPartyId, participantPartyIdList, contactListId, contactListName and isClosed}. The last five are the internal store's, empty here, so an app can merge both stores by sortDate (Mantle's find#InboxThreads). A thread outside trash and junk leaves out its messages there, and one in them shows only those.

parameter.name: searchLimit
parameter.description: How many index matches of the free text one read of the index takes (the newest first); the list reads on past them as it pages

parameter.name: nextBeforeDate
parameter.description: The sortDate of the last row, when hasMore

parameter.name: termList
parameter.description: The operators of searchText, each {operator, value, negate}

parameter.name: searchMode
parameter.description: index or text when searchText had free text

service.description: The messages of a thread the current user may read, oldest first, by any message of it (emailMessageId) or its root (rootEmailMessageId); a message the user may not read is "not found". Each message has its fields (dates in epoch millis; headersString only with includeHeaders), folderKindEnumId, attachmentList, labelList, canSend (the user may send from its account) and unsubscribeMethod (how its List-Unsubscribe header says to unsubscribe: oneClick, mailto or url, null without one; unsubscribe#Message does it). It marks nothing read; set#MessageFlags does.

parameter.name: emailAccountId
parameter.description: The account of the newest message

parameter.name: canSend
parameter.description: The user may reply from the newest message's account

service.description: Internal, for the filing services: the messages they name (emailMessageId, emailMessageIdList, rootEmailMessageId) the current user may change at minLevel (1 read, 2 send), each {emailMessageId, rootEmailMessageId, emailAccountId, emailFolderId, statusId, folderKindEnumId}, or an error before anything changes. accountMap has each account's {emailServerId, folderIdByKind}.

Internal (authorization disabled): queue the server side of a local change of an account with an IMAP server, as EmailRemoteChange rows in the caller's transaction; nothing for any other account or for a message kept only here. changeType flags (flagMap names the flags changed), move (to the message's folder here), labels (stored as IMAP keywords), keywords (addKeywordList, removeKeywordList, such as $Junk), delete (where the message is on the server is kept with the change, as its row goes), sent (APPEND to Sent, unless the server keeps a copy of what it sends), createFolder or renameFolder (emailFolderId). The sync makes them, in order, at the start and end of each session, and right after the commit when email-client sync-push-now is on (the default). A change made from the message's state when applied, so later changes need no merging. fromFolderMap and oldName are accepted for the callers, which ignore its errors.

Sync an account with its IMAP or POP3 server now: a user's "Sync now" (one who reaches the account), or the job and the IDLE workers (authorization disabled). The queued local changes go to the server first; then LIST maps the server's folders (INBOX and the special-use attributes onto the account's folders, never over a kind a user chose with update#EmailFolder), and each subscribed folder (subscribed N is not read), the Inbox first, brings its new mail (within syncWindowDays; at most email-client sync-batch a folder a session), its flags (CONDSTORE CHANGEDSINCE when offered, else a scan every email-client flag-scan minutes) and its expunges (QRESYNC VANISHED, else by UID). A message is stored once, by folder and UID and by Message-ID across folders (a move keeps the row and its links); its files are DbResource files under dbresource://email/; it is threaded by In-Reply-To and References; received mail is ES_RECEIVED, the Sent folder's ES_SENT. The rules run on the new Inbox mail. The email-ECA rules (*.emecas.xml, as poll#EmailServer runs them, with emailAccountId and emailMessageId of the stored row too) run once on each new message as it is stored in the Inbox, each rule in its own transaction, a failing one logged: a Message-ID new to the account (a copy or a move is not new mail), once the account has synced before (the first sync is the mailbox's history), that arrived (IMAP INTERNALDATE, POP3 the Date header) no earlier than a day before the last sync. A POP3 account is fetch-only into the Inbox, by UIDL. Each message, folder and account is on its own: one that fails is logged and the rest go on; a refused sign-in marks the account EasAuthFailed with lastSyncError. No two syncs of an account run at once (syncLockedUntil): a second one reports busy. pushOnly makes only the queued changes; inboxOnly reads the Inbox (and the other folders only when mail left it). A POP3 account of a provider sign-in uses AUTH XOAUTH2.
Live progress for a screen ("Syncing 1,204 of 8,000"): a NotificationMessage on the topic emailSyncProgress to the account's owner and members (not persisted, no alert), at most one a second while a folder has mail to fetch, with {emailAccountId, done, folderCount, foldersDone, folderName, folderPath, folderKept, folderFetched, folderToFetch, folderPending, fetched, toFetch, pending}, and one last with done true, outcome, message and newCount. A session fetches at most email-client sync-batch a folder (folderToFetch); folderPending is all its new mail in the sync window (later sessions bring the rest) and folderKept what was kept of it before, so a first sync shows "{folderKept + folderFetched} of {folderKept + folderPending}" across its sessions; toFetch and pending add up the folders read so far. A sync with nothing to fetch sends none; nothing is sent without a notification socket or cluster peer.

parameter.name: outcome
parameter.description: synced, busy, skipped, paused, failed or authFailed

parameter.name: skippedCount
parameter.description: Messages that did not parse or could not be stored

service.description: The ServiceJob sync_EmailAccounts_frequent: sync each account with an incoming server whose last sync is older than its interval (syncIntervalMinutes, else email-client sync-interval in the conf, 5 minutes; three times as long after an error), or whose last sync stopped at email-client sync-batch with mail left on the server (at every run of the job, so a large first sync goes on a batch a minute), each on its own. Paused accounts, those whose sign-in failed and those syncing now are left.

The servers for an address, for the MailAccounts wizard, within a few seconds: Thunderbird autoconfig (autoconfig.domain, the domain's .well-known URL, then the ISPDB; email-client autoconfig-urls replaces the list), then DNS SRV records (RFC 6186), else the guesses imap.domain and smtp.domain. The best of each, as the fields create#EmailAccount takes, and every one found in incomingList and outgoingList. oauthOnly when the provider signs in only with OAuth. oauthProviderEnumId is the EmailOAuthProvider the mail is at (by the address's domain, the servers found, or the domain's MX hosts: gmail.com, Google Workspace, outlook.com, hotmail.com, live.com, Microsoft 365), whose servers replace the guesses (source provider); oauthConfigured says whether this server is set up to sign in with it, so a wizard offers "Sign in with Google" or "Sign in with Microsoft" only then.

parameter.name: source
parameter.description: autoconfig, ispdb, srv, provider or guess

parameter.name: smtpUsername
parameter.description: When the outgoing server signs in as another user than the incoming one

service.description: Begin the sign-in with Google or Microsoft for a mail account, in a popup (moqui.oauthPopup). For an account the user manages (emailAccountId; its own server, or one is made with the provider's servers) or for a new account (emailAddress with accountName, displayName and accountKindEnumId EakExternal or EakShared), which complete#OAuthSignIn makes once the user signed in: paused (statusId EasPaused, the default) so the sync job leaves it until the app has finished its setup and makes it active (update#EmailAccount), or active at once (EasActive) only with a sync window; syncWindowDays defaults to a year (365, the add-account wizard's), 0 is all mail. statusId and syncWindowDays are for a new account only: an account signing in again keeps its status and window (one whose sign-in failed is active again). oauthProviderEnumId defaults to the account server's, else the address's domain. The state, the PKCE verifier (S256) and a nonce stay in the user's session for ten minutes, bound to the user and the account or address; the redirect URI is the deployment's (email_oauth_redirect_uri), never the request's. The signed-in address must be the account's, unless allowAddressChange (the user confirmed it), which then changes the account's address. Refused when this server is not set up for the provider (get#OAuthProviders). authUrl is what the popup opens; signInId is for get#OAuthStatus.

parameter.name: syncWindowDays
parameter.description: A new account's: default 365, 0 for all mail

parameter.name: statusId
parameter.description: A new account's: EasPaused (the default) or EasActive (with a sync window)

parameter.name: storeProtocol
parameter.description: A new account's: imap (the default) reads its mail on the provider's IMAP server, pop3 on its POP3 server (the provider's popHost; refused when it has none), and the sign-in then also asks for the provider's popScope, which must be granted. The account is made only when the sign-in succeeds. An existing account's server says which it is.

parameter.name: expiresIn
parameter.description: Seconds the sign-in may take

service.description: Internal: the provider's callback, run by the webroot transition /emailOAuth/callback (sendPage sends the popup's page). The state is taken once from the session (unknown, used, another session's or another user's, or older than ten minutes is refused), the code is exchanged with the PKCE verifier, the mail scopes must be granted and the ID token (audience, issuer, expiry, nonce) names the address, which must be the account's (errorCode addressMismatch, unless allowed); then the refresh token is stored encrypted on the account's server (EatOAuth2), the account made or made active again. Every outcome is answered, none is an error: status success or error with errorCode (invalidState, wrongUser, expired, denied, providerError, notConfigured, exchangeFailed, noRefreshToken, scopeNotGranted, noAddress, addressMismatch, storeFailed) and message. The page posts the same (never a token) to its opener on this server's own origin and on the BroadcastChannel moqui-email-oauth.

parameter.name: errorDescription
parameter.description: Shown escaped

service.description: With signInId, how a sign-in of this session ended: status pending, success or error (errorCode and message as complete#OAuthSignIn; unknown when it is gone or another session's or user's), with emailAccountId, emailAddress and expectedAddress, for an opener whose popup could not post back. With emailAccountId (an account the user reaches), its sign-in: authTypeEnumId, oauthProviderEnumId, signedIn, needsSignIn (an EatOAuth2 account with no sign-in or whose sign-in failed: the Inbox rail's Fix), oauthConfigured and signInDate. Never a token.

The OAuth providers (EmailOAuthProvider) and whether this server is set up for each (a client id and secret, not disabled, and a redirect URI), for the wizard's account kinds, with how an address is known to be the provider's mail (addressDomainList, hostSuffixList, mxSuffixList: lower case); redirectUri is the one to register at the providers. No secret is answered.

parameter.name: provider
parameter.description: oauthProviderEnumId, description, configured, addressDomainList, hostSuffixList, mxSuffixList, and the servers of an account made with it: storeHost, storePort, storeProtocol (IMAP), popHost, popPort, popProtocol (empty popHost: no POP account), smtpHost, smtpPort

service.description: The EmailOAuthProvider whose mail an address is, as discover#EmailServer finds it but with no network: the address's domain in addressDomains (gmail.com, outlook.com), else storeHost under a hostSuffixes entry (a company domain whose incoming server is at Google or Microsoft); with lookupMx also the domain's MX hosts under mxSuffixes (Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 on the company's own domain), a DNS query of a few seconds. configured says whether this server is set up to sign in with it (get#OAuthProviders); matchedBy is domain, host or mx. oauthProviderEnumId is empty when no provider has the mail, which is not an error.

Sign an account (manage permission) out of its provider: the refresh token is revoked there when the provider has a revocation endpoint (Google; Microsoft has none), after the commit, best effort and logged, and deleted here; the account waits for a new sign-in (EasAuthFailed). revoked is false when the provider was not asked.

Internal (authorization disabled), for delete#EmailAccount and update#EmailAccount: revoke the sign-in of a server at its provider after the commit (not while another server here signs in as the same address with it, since the provider revokes the whole grant), forget its access token, and with clearToken (the default) delete the refresh token. Failure tolerant: a failure is logged, never an error.

Import .eml files (a message each) and .mbox files into a folder of an account the user may send from (local or synced): file or fileList (uploads), location or locationList (resource locations), or messageText. The messages are kept here only (nothing is appended to the server); one already in the folder by Message-ID is not imported again; one that does not parse or cannot be stored is logged and the rest go on.

A stored message as an RFC 5322 file (.eml) to download, with its EmailMessageAttachment files (inline ones by Content-ID beside the HTML): the mail client keeps no raw message, so the MIME is made again by the send path's builder from the stored fields and headers, as the copy of sent mail appended to Sent (no Bcc). A received message keeps the header block it came with (headersString: Received, Authentication-Results, DKIM-Signature, List-Unsubscribe and the rest, as they came), with the MIME structure of the body made again. A message of an account the user does not reach at read level is "not found"; one with no account only with authorization disabled. A screen sends it with ec.web.sendTextResponse(out.mimeText, out.contentType, out.fileName): the text is the same as mimeBytes (7-bit, unless a received header came 8-bit).

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: The subject made a file name, with .eml

parameter.name: contentType
parameter.description: message/rfc822

service.description: Internal: send the shell counts of the users of these accounts (their owners and members), after a change of their unread mail. Failure tolerant: an error is logged, not returned.
Mark messages (or a thread) read or unread (read permission), flagged or answered (send permission). A flag not given is left as it is.

Move messages (or a thread) to a folder of their own account (send permission). A draft or a message in the Outbox is not moved. Moving to an Archive folder archives (archivedDate), anywhere else unarchives. Local now; the IMAP MOVE is push#RemoteChanges (M5d).
Add and remove labels on messages (or a thread), send permission. A label must be of the message's account.

Hide messages (or a thread) from the inbox until snoozedThruDate, which must be in the future; unsnooze brings them back now. Send permission. return#SnoozedMessages brings them back, unread, when the time comes.

Move messages (or a thread) to their account's Trash folder (send permission). A draft is discarded (deleted). With deleteForever, messages already in Trash are deleted, with their labels and attachments (and the files the client stored under dbresource://email/); one that another record refers to is kept, out of the account. A message in the Outbox is not trashed: cancel#ScheduledSend first.

Internal (authorization disabled): delete messages with their labels, attachment rows and the files the client stored under dbresource://email/. A reply whose parent goes takes the parent's parent; a thread whose root goes takes its oldest remaining message as the root. Fails as a whole when another record refers to one.
Internal (authorization disabled): take messages out of their account, folder, identity and server, kept for the records that refer to them.

actions.script: if (!ec.artifactExecution.authzDisabled()) { ec.message.addError('detach#LocalMessages is internal'); return } const ids = emailMessageIdList.filter((id) => id) if (!ids.length) return ec.entity.find('moqui.basic.email.EmailMessageLabel').condition('emailMessageId', 'in', ids).deleteAll() ec.entity.find('moqui.basic.email.EmailMessage').condition('emailMessageId', 'in', ids) .updateAll({emailAccountId: null, emailFolderId: null, emailIdentityId: null, emailServerId: null, remoteFolderId: null, remoteUid: null})

service.description: Archive messages (or a thread), send permission: those in an Inbox or an ordinary folder move to their account's Archive folder, with archivedDate; Sent, Drafts, Junk and Trash stay where they are. unarchive moves archived ones back to the Inbox.

Create or update a draft (ES_DRAFT) in the Drafts folder of an account the user may send from: emailMessageId for an existing draft (a send that failed becomes a draft again), else a new one in the account of emailIdentityId or emailAccountId. From is the identity (the account's default one when none is given), else the account's address. A field given replaces the draft's; attachmentList (each {attachmentLocation, fileName, fileSize, contentType, contentId, isInline}) replaces its attachments. A reply or forward names parentEmailMessageId, a message the user may read: the draft joins its thread (rootEmailMessageId) and gets the In-Reply-To (not for a forward) and References headers. For an IMAP account the draft is appended to the server's Drafts at the next push (replacing the copy of its last save there), so another client sees it; its send takes it out of Drafts there, and a discard deletes it there.

Send a draft (or retry a send that failed) from an account the user may send from, through the account's server (org.moqui.impl.EmailServices.send#EmailMessage). With a scheduledSendDate in the future it waits in the Outbox as ES_SCHEDULED; with holdSeconds (the undo-send hold) it waits that long; cancel#ScheduledSend takes either back to Drafts, and send#DueDrafts sends it when the time comes. Otherwise it goes now: once sent it is in the Sent folder (and the message it answers is marked answered); a send that fails waits in the Outbox (ES_READY) with sendError, for a retry. It runs in one transaction, the caller's when there is one, so a draft saved earlier in the same transaction sends.
Take a message waiting in the Outbox back to Drafts: a scheduled send, the undo-send hold, or a send that failed. Send permission. One that is sending or sent already is refused.

Internal (authorization disabled): move a message from one of fromStatusIdList to toStatusId (ES_SCHEDULED with its scheduledSendDate, or ES_READY to send now) under a row lock, out of its folder (the Outbox), and set its server from its account. claimed is false when its status was not one of them, as when another send or a cancel got there first.

actions.script: claimed = false if (!ec.artifactExecution.authzDisabled()) { ec.message.addError('claim#DraftSend is internal'); return } const from = fromStatusIdList && fromStatusIdList.length ? fromStatusIdList : ['ES_DRAFT', 'ES_READY'] const message = ec.entity.find('moqui.basic.email.EmailMessage').condition('emailMessageId', emailMessageId).forUpdate(true).one() if (message == null || !from.includes(message.statusId)) return // a Ready message without an error is being sent if (message.statusId === 'ES_READY' && !message.sendError) return const account = message.emailAccountId ? ec.entity.find('moqui.basic.email.EmailAccount').condition('emailAccountId', message.emailAccountId).one() : null message.setFields({statusId: toStatusId, emailFolderId: null, sendError: null, scheduledSendDate: toStatusId === 'ES_SCHEDULED' ? scheduledSendDate : message.scheduledSendDate, messageDate: toStatusId === 'ES_SCHEDULED' ? scheduledSendDate : ec.user.nowTimestamp, emailServerId: account?.emailServerId || message.emailServerId}, true, null, null) message.update() claimed = true

service.description: Internal (authorization disabled), for send#Draft and send#DueDrafts: claim the message (claim#DraftSend to ES_READY, from fromStatusIdList), send it (org.moqui.impl.EmailServices.send#EmailMessage), then record the result (record#SendResult), all in one transaction: send#EmailMessage writes a client message's Sent status in it and gives its failures as sendError, not as errors. An error of the send itself rolls the claim back, so the message is as it was.

actions.script: sent = false claimed = false messageId = null sendError = null statusId = null if (!ec.artifactExecution.authzDisabled()) { ec.message.addError('deliver#DraftMessage is internal'); return } const claim = ec.service.sync().name('org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.claim#DraftSend').parameters({ emailMessageId: emailMessageId, fromStatusIdList: fromStatusIdList, toStatusId: 'ES_READY'}).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return claimed = claim.claimed === true if (!claimed) return const result = ec.service.sync().name('org.moqui.impl.EmailServices.send#EmailMessage').parameter('emailMessageId', emailMessageId).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return messageId = result?.messageId || null sendError = result?.sendError || (messageId ? null : 'The message was not sent') const recorded = ec.service.sync().name('org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.record#SendResult').parameters({ emailMessageId: emailMessageId, messageId: messageId, sendError: sendError}).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return sent = sendError == null statusId = recorded.statusId ?? null if (!sent) ec.logger.warn(`Email message ${emailMessageId} was not sent: ${sendError}`)

service.description: Internal (authorization disabled): after send#EmailMessage, a sent message goes to its account's Sent folder, read, dated when it was sent, and the message it replies to is marked answered; one that failed stays in the Outbox (ES_READY, no folder) with sendError.

Send the messages whose time has come: scheduled sends and undo-send holds (ES_SCHEDULED, scheduledSendDate past), the oldest first. The ServiceJob send_DueDrafts_frequent runs it every minute. A client may also send its own held message as soon as the hold ends: emailMessageId, send permission, due. Each message is on its own: one that fails is logged, waits in the Outbox with its error, and the rest go on.

Bring back the snoozed messages whose time has come: their snoozedThruDate is cleared and the newest message of each thread is marked unread, so the thread is back in the inbox as new. The ServiceJob return_SnoozedMessages_frequent runs it every minute. Each thread is on its own: one that fails is logged and the rest go on.
Internal (authorization disabled), for return#SnoozedMessages: clear the snooze of these messages and mark unreadEmailMessageId unread.

Internal (authorization disabled), for the sync after the rules: new mail in a snoozed thread brings the thread back now, as Gmail does: the snooze of the thread's messages in the account is cleared, so the thread is in the Inbox with the new (unread) message. Only received mail still in the Inbox wakes a thread (not mail the rules moved or marked as spam). Each thread is on its own: one that fails is logged and the rest go on.

A user's unread email (the current user's; another user's only with authorization disabled, as get#ShellCounts does): the messages in the Inbox folders of their accounts that are unread, not snoozed and not archived. unreadThreadCount counts their threads, accountCountMap each account's. For the shell counts' email part (Mantle's get#ShellCounts).

Internal, for create#EmailRule, update#EmailRule and test#EmailRule: the conditions and actions of a rule checked and in their stored form, or an error saying what is wrong. A conditionsJson or actionsJson text is read as the list. conditionsOnly checks only the conditions (a rule tried before it has actions).

Internal, for the rule services: whether the current user may change a rule: its owner, or a manager of its account. level is the user's on the rule's account (3 for a rule on all of the owner's accounts).

The rules the current user may change, in order: their own, and those on the accounts they manage (emailAccountId for one account's, which also lists the user's rules on all accounts). Each has its fields, conditionList, actionList, accountName (null for all accounts) and isOwner.
A rule of the current user: on emailAccountId (which they must manage), or on all their own accounts. It goes after their other rules unless sequenceNum is given.
Change a rule (its owner, or a manager of its account). A field given is set; the conditions and actions are replaced when given.
Delete a rule (its owner, or a manager of its account).
Put rules in this order (each the user may change): their sequenceNum becomes 10, 20, 30 and on.

Run the rules of an account on messages: on the mail the sync just stored (emailAccountId and emailMessageIdList, internal: authorization disabled), or on demand over a folder (emailFolderId, send permission on its account; emailRuleId for one rule, limit the newest messages, 2000 by default). The rules are those on the account and its owner's on all accounts, enabled, in order; a matched rule's actions run and its matchedCount goes up; stopProcessing ends the rules for that message. Drafts and the Outbox are left. A rule that fails is logged and skipped, and the others go on. The server side of what the actions change goes through push#RemoteChanges.
dryRun (test#EmailRule) changes nothing: no action runs and no matchedCount goes up, read permission on the folder's account is enough, and matchList is each message a rule matched ({emailMessageId, subject, fromAddress, fromName, messageDate, snippet, emailRuleIdList}, newest first), with testedCount. With conditionsJson (normalized) and matchAllEnumId, a dry run tries that rule, not yet saved, alone.

Try a rule on an account's recent mail without acting on it: a saved rule (emailRuleId, one the user may change; its conditions and match, or those given here to try an edit) or a rule not yet saved (conditionList or conditionsJson, and matchAllEnumId), over the newest limit messages (50 by default, at most 1000) of a folder: emailFolderId, else the Inbox of emailAccountId, else of the rule's account. Read permission on the folder's account; drafts and the Outbox are left out. Nothing changes: no action runs and the rule's matchedCount stays (run#EmailRules with dryRun). matchList is each message it matches ({emailMessageId, subject, fromAddress, fromName, messageDate, snippet}, newest first, with what opens it in the Inbox: store email, threadId and rootEmailMessageId (its thread's root, as find#Messages answers them), emailAccountId and emailFolderId), with matchedCount and testedCount.

Spam: move messages (or a thread) to their account's Junk folder (send permission), with the IMAP keyword $Junk where the server keeps keywords, so a server that learns from it does. notSpam moves those in Junk back to the Inbox with $NotJunk. Drafts and the Outbox are left.

Block a sender: a rule of the current user on the account (which they must manage) that moves mail from that address to Junk and stops the other rules, and the message given to Junk now (report#Spam). The address is the sender of emailMessageId, or emailAddress with emailAccountId. A sender blocked already gets no second rule.

Unsubscribe from the list a message came from, by its List-Unsubscribe header (RFC 2369), the way it offers: - oneClick: with List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click (RFC 8058) and an https address, a POST of List-Unsubscribe=One-Click to it from the server (no cookies, no referrer); a 2xx answer is done. A POST that fails (or an address on a private network, which is refused) is logged and the next way is tried. - mailto: a message to the mailto address (its subject and body from the address, else "unsubscribe"), sent from the message's account (send permission); it is in Sent after. - url: the http or https address for the client to open (the list's own page), when neither of the others could be done. Read permission for the url, send permission for the others. A message without the header is an error.

parameter.name: method
parameter.description: oneClick, mailto or url

parameter.name: unsubscribed
parameter.description: Done here (oneClick or mailto); false for url

parameter.name: url
parameter.description: For url: the address for the client to open

parameter.name: postError
parameter.description: Why the one-click POST did not do it, when it was tried

service.description: An address an account sends as (manage permission); isDefault makes it the account's default.
Change an identity (manage permission). A field given is set, an empty one cleared; isDefault true makes it the default.
Delete an identity (manage permission); its drafts send as the account's default identity.

Which of these addresses are contacts of a user (the current user; another user only with authorization disabled), for an automatic reply to contacts only. The framework keeps no contacts (they are the app's, such as Mantle's parties), so it asks a hook service, as the shell counts do: the one the email_contact_service property names, else the theme value STRT_EMAIL_CONTACT_SERVICE of the user's qapps theme. The hook is called with authorization disabled, in a transaction of its own (one that fails leaves the caller's as it was), with userId and emailAddressList and answers contactAddressList: those that are on a party the user can see as a contact. contactAddressList is null when no hook is configured (every sender then counts as a contact); a hook that fails or answers no list is logged once by name, hookFailed is true and the list is empty. Lower case, only addresses asked about.

An account's automatic reply (read permission); outOfOffice is null when it has none. isActive is whether it is on now. replyAudienceEnumId is who gets it (EraEveryone when none was chosen); internalDomains the more domains whose senders are internal (a comma list); contactHookService the hook that says who is a contact for EraContacts (null when none is configured: every sender is one).

Set an account's automatic reply (manage permission; not the Internal account). replyAudienceEnumId is who gets it: EraEveryone (the default), EraContacts (internal senders and the owner's contacts, as filter#ContactAddresses says; every sender when no contact hook is configured) or EraInternal (internal senders only). An internal sender is a user of this system, at the domain of a hosted or shared account, or at one of internalDomains: more domains of the organization, separated by commas or spaces (a leading @ is dropped); they are stored in lower case, comma separated.

Internal (authorization disabled), for the sync after the rules: the account's automatic reply (EmailOutOfOffice, while it is enabled and between its dates) to the senders of its new Inbox mail, through the account's server like a message the user sends (it is in Sent after), as RFC 3834 asks: - once per sender in replyOncePerDays (4 by default; EmailOutOfOfficeSent), and only to mail received since the reply was turned on (its fromDate, else when it was stored) and in the last 7 days, so a first sync of old mail answers nothing; - only to mail sent to the account (its address or one of its identities in To or Cc), not to Bcc or a list; - never to a list or bulk mail (List-Id, List-Unsubscribe, List-Post, Precedence bulk, list or junk), to another automatic message (Auto-Submitted other than no, X-Auto-Response-Suppress, X-Autoreply, X-Autorespond), to a bounce (an empty Return-Path), to a no-reply or system address (mailer-daemon, postmaster, noreply, no-reply, donotreply, bounce), to the account itself, or to spam (mail the rules moved to Junk or Trash); - with Auto-Submitted: auto-replied and X-Auto-Response-Suppress: All, and In-Reply-To and References to the mail it answers (not threaded with it, and the mail is not marked answered); - with internalBodyHtml, when set, to an internal sender: a user of this system (by email address) or an address at the domain of a hosted or shared account or at one of the reply's internalDomains (the organization's own domains); - to the reply's audience (replyAudienceEnumId): everyone; internal senders and the owner's contacts (EraContacts: filter#ContactAddresses asks the app's hook, the email_contact_service property or the theme value STRT_EMAIL_CONTACT_SERVICE; with no hook every sender counts as a contact, and a hook that fails counts none, logged); or internal senders only (EraInternal). The subject is the reply's own, else "Automatic reply: " and the mail's subject. Each message is on its own: one that fails is logged and the rest go on.
The text blocks the current user may use in the composer: their own and those shared with a user group they are in now; searchText matches the title, the shortcut or the body.

actions.script: const cf = ec.entity.conditionFactory textBlockList = [] const userId = ec.user.userId if (!userId) return const groupIds = Array.from(ec.entity.find('moqui.security.UserGroupMember').condition('userId', userId) .conditionDate('fromDate', 'thruDate', null).disableAuthz().list()).map((row) => row.userGroupId) const reach = [cf.makeCondition('ownerUserId', 'equals', userId)] if (groupIds.length) reach.push(cf.makeCondition('userGroupId', 'in', groupIds)) let find = ec.entity.find('moqui.basic.email.EmailTextBlock').condition(cf.makeCondition(reach, 'or')) if (searchText) find = find.condition(cf.makeCondition(['title', 'shortcut', 'bodyHtml'] .map((field) => cf.makeCondition(field, 'like', `%${searchText}%`, false, true)), 'or')) textBlockList = Array.from(find.orderBy('title').list()).map((row) => ({emailTextBlockId: row.emailTextBlockId, ownerUserId: row.ownerUserId ?? null, userGroupId: row.userGroupId ?? null, title: row.title ?? null, shortcut: row.shortcut ?? null, bodyHtml: row.bodyHtml ?? null, isOwner: row.ownerUserId === userId, isShared: !!row.userGroupId}))

service.description: A text block of the current user; userGroupId shares it with a group the user is in.
Change a text block of the current user's (its owner only). An empty userGroupId makes it personal again.
Delete a text block of the current user's (its owner only).
The current user's saved searches, for the Inbox rail.

actions.script: searchList = [] if (!ec.user.userId) return searchList = Array.from(ec.entity.find('moqui.basic.email.EmailSearch').condition('ownerUserId', ec.user.userId) .orderBy('sequenceNum,searchName').list()).map((row) => ({emailSearchId: row.emailSearchId, searchName: row.searchName ?? null, queryText: row.queryText ?? null, sequenceNum: row.sequenceNum ?? null}))

service.description: Save a search of the current user: a new one, or emailSearchId changed.

actions.script: if (!ec.user.userId) { ec.message.addError('No user for the saved search'); return } let row if (emailSearchId) { row = ec.entity.find('moqui.basic.email.EmailSearch').condition('emailSearchId', emailSearchId).one() if (row == null || row.ownerUserId !== ec.user.userId) { ec.message.addError(`Saved search ${emailSearchId} not found`); return } row.setFields({searchName: searchName, queryText: queryText, sequenceNum: sequenceNum}, true, null, null) row.update() return } row = ec.entity.makeValue('moqui.basic.email.EmailSearch') row.setSequencedIdPrimary() row.setFields({ownerUserId: ec.user.userId, searchName: searchName, queryText: queryText, sequenceNum: sequenceNum}, false, null, null) row.create() emailSearchId = row.emailSearchId

service.description: Delete a saved search of the current user's.
